record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: Let L be positive and continuous on C^2, and call an entire function H of bounded L-index in direction c when finitely many normalized directional derivatives |D_c^k H(z)|/(k! L(z)^k), 0 <= k <= m0, dominate every normalized order m at every point. Suppose P1(z1,z2) and P2(z1,z2) are entire functions of bounded L-index in the coordinate directions (1,0) and (0,1), respectively. For the equation P1(z1,z2) partial F/partial z1 + P2(z1,z2) partial F/partial z2 = h(z1,z2), what direction b and what additional assumptions imply that an entire solution F has bounded L-index in direction b?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. For a nonzero direction $c\in\mathbb{C}^2$, write $D_c H(z):=\sum_{j=1}^{2}c_j\,\partial H/\partial z_j(z)$ and inductively $D_c^k H = D_c(D_c^{k-1}H)$. An entire function $H:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $c$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_0$ such that for every $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and every $z\in\mathbb{C}^2$,
$$\frac{|D_c^m H(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\ \le\ \max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|D_c^k H(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}.$$
The least such $m_0$ is the $L$-index of $H$ in direction $c$.

Let $P_1(z_1,z_2)$ and $P_2(z_1,z_2)$ be entire functions such that $P_1$ is of bounded $L$-index in direction $(1,0)$ and $P_2$ is of bounded $L$-index in direction $(0,1)$, and let $h:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be entire. Consider the first-order linear PDE
$$P_1(z_1,z_2)\,\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_1}(z_1,z_2)\ +\ P_2(z_1,z_2)\,\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_2}(z_1,z_2)\ =\ h(z_1,z_2).$$

Determine a direction $b\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ and additional sufficient conditions on $P_1$, $P_2$, $h$, and $L$ such that every entire solution $F$ of this equation has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$.

artifact.status_search_result: Related works address sufficient conditions for boundedness of L-index in a direction for entire solutions of certain linear PDEs (including second-order equations and compositions), but no source verifies a definitive resolution of this specific first-order coordinate PDE problem with the stated hypotheses on P1 and P2. Status appears unresolved in full generality.
